name: Council
tagline: What council has decided, what it is deciding next, and the record that connects decisions to everything else in this dashboard.
primer: Council is the connective tissue of this dashboard. Nearly every figure in the other six domains exists because council voted for something: a levy, a capital project, a service level, a by-law. The decision record is where a number stops being a fact about the township and becomes a choice someone made, on a date, for reasons written down in a staff report.

An Ontario municipal council acts only by resolution or by-law, and only at a properly constituted meeting. Individual members, including the head of council, have no authority to direct staff or commit the municipality. The head of council chairs, sets no policy alone, and has one vote. This is the single most important thing to understand before governing: the job is building majorities and setting agendas, not issuing instructions.

The staff report is the instrument that actually shapes decisions. It states the recommendation, the background, the financial implications, and the alternatives considered. Reading the report rather than the minutes is the difference between knowing what was decided and knowing why. A decision that departs from the staff recommendation is worth flagging in the record — not because staff are always right, but because the departure is where council exercised independent judgement and the reasons are worth knowing.

Meetings are open by default. The Municipal Act permits closed sessions only for enumerated purposes — land acquisition or disposition, litigation and solicitor-client privilege, personal matters about identifiable individuals, labour relations, and a short list of others — and the resolution to close must state which. A rising share of business conducted in closed session is a measurable and neutral fact about how a council operates.

The strategic plan states council's priorities. Whether those priorities carry measures is a separate question from whether they are the right priorities, and the absence of measures is a finding worth recording plainly: it means progress cannot be evidenced, only asserted. Where a strategic priority has a measure, this dashboard links it to the indicator that tracks it.

Township council members also sit on county council, which decides county roads, paramedic services, social services, and several planning approvals affecting the township. A complete picture of what a North Glengarry council member votes on requires both agendas, and the decision record here labels which body made each decision.

gaps: Vote records are only available where a recorded vote was requested or is required. Many decisions carry no recorded vote, in which case the record shows the resolution as carried without member-level detail. That absence should be shown as an absence, not filled in.
Staff report numbering and agenda formats change between clerks and between council terms, which makes automated extraction unreliable and manual entry the realistic path.
Closed session subject matter is recorded only at the level of the enumerated exception cited. The share of business conducted in closed session is measurable; its substance is not.

indicators.name: Decisions recorded in this dashboard
indicators.definition: Count of council decisions transcribed into the decision record below, by year of decision. This measures the completeness of this dashboard's own record, not council's activity. It exists so that coverage is visible: a thin year here means transcription is outstanding, not that council was idle.

indicators.name: Share of meetings including a closed session
indicators.definition: Percentage of regular council meetings in the year that included at least one closed session. Closed sessions are permitted for the purposes enumerated in the Municipal Act and the resolution to close must state the applicable exception. This figure counts occurrence; it does not evaluate whether any closure was appropriate.

indicators.name: Strategic priorities carrying a stated measure
indicators.definition: Percentage of the strategic plan's stated priorities that carry an explicit, checkable measure of progress. A priority without a measure can be advanced or abandoned without either being demonstrable. This describes the plan as written; it does not assess whether the priorities themselves are well chosen.

tables.title: Strategic Plan 2023-2027: pillars and stated measures
tables.description: The plan adopted in March 2023 for the current council term is built on three pillars — GROW, FOSTER and CHAMPION — resting on a stated foundation of human resources, information technology, financial stability and corporate values. The pillars are recorded here as written. Whether each carries a checkable measure is a separate question from whether the pillars are the right ones, and is answered by reading the plan.

The measures column is deliberately left as unconfirmed rather than filled in: recording 'no stated measure' would be a claim about the document that has not been verified page by page, and this dashboard does not make claims it has not checked. The linked indicator column is this dashboard's own choice of proxy, which is analysis rather than council's position.
